one_liner: Asana has a broad REST API (OpenAPI-described) with OAuth 2.0 and self-serve personal access tokens; the vendor-hosted MCP server is plausible but not confirmed by the supplied pages.
auth_notes: OAuth recommended when multiple users sign in. PATs are generated in the developer console. Service Accounts are long-lived tokens, Enterprise tier only, and super-admin created.
access_notes: PATs and OAuth apps are created self-serve from the developer console. The supplied pages do not explicitly state that a free plan includes API access, and the draft's 150 req/min and paid-only endpoint claims were not found on them. A Developer Sandbox Terms document exists.
blocker_notes: Service accounts are Enterprise only; this does not block PAT or OAuth use. The free-tier API limits could not be verified from the supplied pages.

evidence.quote: Asana's API is a REST interface that speaks JSON at `https://app.asana.com/api/1.0`
This reference is generated from our [OpenAPI Specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Asana/openapi/master/defs/asana_oas.yaml)
Automate tedious work in powerful, bespoke ways with our platform features like rule actions, webhooks, and our API.
This is the best choice if multiple users need to sign in to your app.
Service Accounts are an [Enterprise tier](https://asana.com/enterprise) feature
You create a personal access token from your own account's developer settings
